stories.title: A bakery, a playground, a speaker’s corner … how a former Brussels car garage tore up the art gallery rulebook
stories.summary: Repurposing a space previously used for selling Citroëns, the Belgian capital now has its first ever dedicated space for contemporary art. It’s certainly ambitious – but will they be able to fill it? ‘A cathedral of cars” is how the colossal Citroën garage in Brussels was described when it opened in 1934, conceived as a startling glass temple to showcase the streamlined wonders of the automobile age. It greeted the street with an immense curtain wall of glass that wrapped a monumental nave-like showroom, culminating in a curved art deco prow, which glowed like a crystal lantern by night. Almost a century later, arts and culture have replaced cars as the great urban consumables of our age. Consequently, after a €230m decade-long transformation in collaboration with the Pompidou Centre, this gargantuan garage has been reborn as a palace of performance, dance, music, film, architecture and visual art. The original Parisian Pompidou was designed as a transformable cultural machine for the city ; this place takes those urban ambitions to an even greater extreme. Continue reading...

stories.title: ‘I am scared’: Careless People author Sarah Wynn-Williams on living under a gag order - and why it’s time to speak out against big tech
stories.summary: Since writing her bestselling exposé, the former employee has been forbidden from speaking publicly about Meta. In an exclusive extract from her Orwell lecture, she talks about corporate lawfare, and the growing backlash against NDAs George Orwell understood that what is missing often tells you more than what is there. In Nineteen Eighty-Four, there is a slot in the wall covered by a wire grate. They call it the memory hole. When a document becomes inconvenient to the authorities – a photograph that contradicts the official line, a newspaper that remembers the wrong promise, a name that is no longer supposed to exist – you simply feed it into the slot, whereupon it is whirled away on a current of warm air to enormous hidden furnaces where it burns. The Party doesn’t argue with the past. It removes it. Controlling the past is one of its central tools of power: “Who controls the past controls the future: who controls the present controls the past.” Continue reading...

stories.title: Trump claims revised economic data shows pre-midterms figures were ‘fake’ | First Thing
stories.summary: President calls for investigation after GDP figures were adjusted upwards, despite revisions to official economic figures being commonplace. Plus, the weird and macabre world of Victorian Christmas cards Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here Good morning. Donald Trump has alleged without evidence that economic figures published by the US federal government before this month’s midterm elections were “fake” and demanded an investigation after voters roundly rejected his Republican party. In a holiday message on his Truth Social platform, the US president wished a happy Thanksgiving “to even those who issued fake Economic Numbers, just prior to the Election, and corrected them yesterday, three weeks late, showing that the GDP was actually 4.3%, versus 3.4%”. Why did Trump call the figures fake? Revisions to official economic figures are commonplace, but Trump has tried repeatedly to challenge trust in economic data that does not support his claims that a historic boom is under way in the US. “Why wasn’t the correct number issued before the Election? I am asking for an immediate investigation of this situation,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform. “This is not a small error, this is a massive, and purposeful, error”. What other acerbic well-wishes did Trump offer? He wished “a very Happy Thanksgiving to all of those people that have worked so hard to bring our Country to the Radical Far Left” as well as “those who want to redistribute Property, so that all of the hardworking people that have built up, over a lifetime, a certain Wealth, will now be forced to distribute it throughout the Country, even to those who refuse to work”. Why are the ballots at the center of an ongoing dispute over the 2020 election? Some Republicans, led by Trump, claimed the election results had been rigged despite Joe Biden being certified after several recounts. Republican state officials had refused to overturn the result, despite a now-infamous phone call from Trump to pressure the Georgia secretary of state, Brad Raffensperger, to “find 11,780 votes”. Tiny Hat: a new Linux distro dedicated to retro gamedev
stories.summary: Tiny Hat uses only around 100MB of RAM after booting, and can be booted from a >= 1GB memory stick. It comes with a few small games, an easy way to install and run more games and several example programs for getting into retro game development. It also uses a modern stack of libraries, with dwl / Wayland, SDL3 and GTK4. One possible use is to buy a cheap x86 machine for younger members of a family, to completely brain wash inspire them into getting into graphics programming and appreciating retro games, perhaps as a Christmas present. At least a few people have found it fun so far, so I wanted to share it. Comments

stories.title: sqlite3_rsync: Database Remote-Copy Tool For SQLite
stories.summary: sqlite3_rsync: Database Remote-Copy Tool For SQLite This additional SQLite tool has been around for a while now - it was added as "experimental" in SQLite 3.47.0 in October 2024 and enhanced in SQLite 3.50.0 in May 2025 . It was only today that I understood one of its most attractive characteristics. Normally, if you want to grab a snapshot copy of a SQLite database, you need to use either the backup API or VACUUM INTO . In both cases you need enough disk space to create a duplicate copy of your database, so if you're on a small instance and you already use more than half of the available disk you are plain out of luck. sqlite3_rsync can copy a snapshot of your database over an SSH connection to another machine, without first needing to create a full local copy! It's also good for synchronizing an existing copy of a database without re-transmitting the entire thing over the network. It works in a similar way to regular rsync: The core idea behind the protocol is that the replica sends cryptographic hashes for pages or groups of pages over to the origin side. The origin sends back page content that differs, or requests finer-grain hashes if a multi-page hash does not match. If the origin and replica start out being vastly different, the total network bandwidth can exceed the size of the entire database, due to the overhead of exchanging hashes, but the excess bandwidth is not great - a few percent at most. Update : Hah! Turns out I wrote about this application of sqlite_rsync back in October 2024 when the tool was first released. Tags: backups , sqlite

stories.title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
stories.summary: My comment on The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features — Hacker News. I had a NYT photographer take my picture at my home earlier this year (for a story about Moltbook, oddly enough). At one point I asked if they could fix things up if I had a stain on my shirt and they said absolutely not - they present photographs as they were taken, with cropping and balancing applied but no edits beyond that. He did spend a bunch of time trying to find the best possible natural lighting for the shots he wanted. The photo at the top of https://www.nytimes.com/2026/02/02/technology/moltbook-ai-so... is my laptop, taken in my garden, after hunting around for the best spot that didn't have too much glare on the screen. You can see how dirty my screen is, too! Photography for a newspaper is photo journalism, and they take it seriously. (Thankfully I did not have a visible stain on my shirt.) Tags: photography , new-york-times , hacker-news , journalism
